verbalization: The visible evidence suggests that Dofequidar may interact with the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex through its targets, which are macrophage scavenger receptor types I and II. These receptors are identified as targets of multiple compounds, including 6-Methoxykaempferol-3-O-Alpha-L-Rhamnopyranosyl-(1->6)-Beta-D-Glucopyranoside, [3-(3-Hydroxy-4,5-dimethoxyphenyl)-3-oxopropyl] acetate, and (Z)-Calacorene. All three compounds are predicted to have a final score of 0.5561, indicating a moderate level of confidence in their interaction with the target complex. The shared pathway from Dofequidar to the macrophage scavenger receptors and then to the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex suggests a potential mechanism involving the modulation of macrophage function or the regulation of gene expression through these receptors. The evidence supports a possible role for Dofequidar in influencing the activity of the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction.
